utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. The affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence still applies, Mr. Brakovic. And Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Brakovic. I would like to ask you, and indeed to ask me more than anyone else, to wait for the end of my question before answering -- well, they taught me a little trick. You look at the transcript, and then when you see that the transcript is finished, that the cursor is no longer moving, then you can start giving me your answer. Mr. Brakovic, am I right if I say that from the 24th of March, 1999, until the end of the war you saw General Vlastimir Djordjevic for the first time after the signing of the Kumanovo Agreement in June when he was escorting Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that period I saw General Djordjevic at a meeting in Pristina after the signing of the Kumanovo Agreement. I think that the agenda of the meeting was the implementation of this agreement insofar as it pertained to the police forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that from the 24th of March, 1999, until the end of the war you never saw General Djordjevic in the field in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I answered your question with my previous answer, but if you ask me again, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that from the beginning of 1999 until the 24th of March, you saw General Djordjevic at a meeting in the staff of the ministry when he was escorting General, or rather, the Minister of the Interior Vlajko Stojiljkovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said in my previous testimony that I had an opportunity to see General Djordjevic at meetings and in the field. If I'm not mistaken, there was this meeting on the 17th of February, and it is only logical to say that I saw him there -- well, there are no minutes that would indicate that we met at any previous meetings during that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, the department of the police in the Pristina SUP, the one that you headed, had two police stations, general-duty police stations, and there was also the railway security police station, the round-the-clock duty police station, and security police station; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the police station that you are talking about was called the duty and interventions police station, so that was the more precise name. But what you say is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And please do correct me when I'm not entirely precise. Am I right that you were the immediate superior of the police station commanders which were part of your department of the interior or the department of the police?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that within the department of the police in the Pristina SUP, there was a section for PJP training, the section for reserve police force, and the section for defence preparations and mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct in part. There were no sections; there were agents, officers, within the department who were in charge of those areas that you listed. So those were not sections but individual policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Inspectors who were in charge of those areas that I listed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please explain to us a little bit this -- the police station for security, what was its purview?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security police station, if the memory serves me right and I think it does, provided security to MUP facilities, the facilities of the Ministry of the Interior in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Your police department in the Pristina SUP, did it also deal with providing security to various persons from police or other officials who came to Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not part of the system. We didn't have people within the system assigned to those tasks; but on several occasions we were asked to provide security to some persons, and then we set up a team of about ten people who did that work. I don't think that this group of people was part of the security police station, but this section was set up with people who were good and who had the affinity to that kind of work. But we wanted to make that part of the system and have them be part of the security police station, but we didn't manage to do that because the events unfolded as they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the head of the police department in the Pristina SUP, were you supposed to be notified about any visits by minister of the interior, deputy ministers, or any other officials who would come into the territory covered by the Pristina SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, the logic dictated that I should be notified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, am I right if I say that you, as the head of the police department, were not the superior officer of the police station commanders that were part of the OUP, for instance, in Podujevo, in Glogovac, in Kosovo Polje, and Obilic that were organisational units of the Pristina SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that you, as the head of the police department in the Pristina SUP, that you issued instructive dispatches to the police stations that were part of the OUP but that were organisational units within the Pristina SUP, such as, for instance, Glogovac, Podujevo, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you are not right. In order to send a dispatch to department of the interior, OUP, the chief of the secretariat had to do that. If I needed to do so within my sphere of work, which was police, anything that would be of instructive nature or anything of that sort, if I had to send something like that to somebody in the department of the interior, that dispatch had to be signed by the chief of the secretariat who signed it and addressed it to the chief of the OUP and the chief of the OUP then notified all those he felt should be notified with the contents of the dispatch. So this is how the system functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And am I right that you prepared the instructive dispatch for the SUP chief and then he would forward it to the OUPs that were organisational units of the Pristina SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that instructive dispatches did not have the force of an order issued by a superior but were simply an instruction on how laws or tasks should be implemented and carried out?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you could say that. The very word "instructive" tells you that it is a document of the nature that you specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me be more specific, those instructive dispatches tell people how to do something and not so much what to do?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, please feel free to say it better. I defer to your authority.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as a rule, you defined it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the police acts in accordance with the law and regulations, so it is not necessary to stress all the time what should be done because you have the tasks that are defined by the law on the Ministry of the Interior, the police, and then the police is duty-bound to do those tasks autonomously. And the instructive dispatches would draw people's attention to some elements, instruct them how to organise the performance of some tasks, to facilitate their execution. Let me just be as specific as I can, that would be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that the police administration sent out instructive dispatches to the Pristina SUP chief regarding the line of work that pertained to the tasks of the police department?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not as regards the work of the police department, but work of the uniformed police force, what we call the general-duty police. Since it did not pertain to the traffic police, because they had their own line of work, and they had different focus; so the police sent the dispatches to the SUP chief, and then he decided what he should tell me as head of the department and what to tell other people so that everybody is kept abreast with the tasks because the police work is both complex and compatible. It is impossible to have an instruction deal with just one segment of the police. The logic dictates that several segments must be brought together in the execution of a task.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right when I say that police stations for the most part carried out tasks in accordance with their monthly and daily plans?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the most part, yes; but for another part, no, because the police work is so unpredictable that you can't even predict what you would be doing in an hour because various incidents happen that you could not have predicted. So you do your work in accordance with the plan, daily or monthly plans which are clearly defined, but there is always this element of the unexpected.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brakovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have on our screens Exhibit D001-2917.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, do you see this document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is the instruction on the execution of the tasks of the interior from the purview of the Ministry of the Interior on the part of the reserve force. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please ask you what is the year of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you now it's 1998. It's the decision of the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 2, or rather, page 3 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Djurdjic, we don't have the document on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't have it, but I thought that you had it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I think that you have the document in front of you now.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I actually had it right from the start.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have page 3 in B/C/S and page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, you can see that this is the directive of the 22nd of June, 1998. It was issued by Minister Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Djurdjic. What is the relevance you see of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance lies in the fact that this is the foundation for adducing the order on the engagement of the reserve force within the ministry. So this is an instruction or directive pursuant to Article 7 of the Law on the Interior. The chief issues an instruction, and this is the foundation for the reserve force; and then we have orders every six months in July and December 1998, and this is the foundation. And that was the foundation for the reserve force to be deployed by the SUPs in the territory of Serbia and the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What provision in the order do you refer to in particular?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is a general, let me tell you, you have the manner of execution of tasks; the basis for the deployment or use; the whole order, how to plan, organise, and coordinate the work. These are -- you can see there is the final provisions. "The chief of the secretariat shall direct and coordinate the work and is responsible," item 4, and within the secretariat of the Pristina SUP there is an inspector, as we heard from the witness, who deals with this on a daily basis, regarding mobilisation, defence preparations, and the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it paragraph 2 that you rely on in particular?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm relying on all the paragraphs in this instruction or directive because this is the legal basis, and let me just tell you what is the basis for the Pristina SUP, that would be paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Either the document speaks for itself or the witness needs to indicate to us the significance he sees in the document. At the moment I was trying to see whether the document spoke for itself, but your having to explain at great length I think it should be a matter for the witness. But before you do, I see Mr. Hannis on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That does address one point I was going to raise. Paragraph 2 does seem to talk about engaging the reserve forces during peacetime. I'm not sure how that is pertinent to the war time aspect of our case. But secondly, I have sort of a foundational concern: I see at the end of the page where we have the minister's stamp and signature, we also have hand printed the document number and date. That's not the way I've seen it on some of the other orders from the minister. Oftentimes part of that is typed and then the number is handwritten but not the whole thing, and the xeroxed copy I have causes me to have some questions about whether or not that's something that's been added later or even possibly changed. I don't know where this document came from. Some of these types of documents that we had, we got pursuant to RFA request to the government authorities in Serbia, but I don't know the providence of this one; and I wanted to raise that issue before we went too far down the road with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we will look at two documents that are listed under 65 ter, and I'm not sure whether I received this from the National Council when I went through the archives of the office of the minister or was it something that was used under 65 ter. But we have two more documents for sure, orders on specific use of forces where you can see in the stamp of the ministry the reference numbers of the log-book, in the log-book of the ministry. But I'm not, of course, opposed to providing Mr. Hannis with the full disclosure as to where I got this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, if you could attend to that as soon as you can, but in the meantime the witness may be able to tell us something of his understanding of the document, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, could you please explain this direction on the method of carrying out interior duties dated 26th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, could I please just take a look at the first page of this document. This directive explains in detail the performance of internal affairs duties by reserve forces. It regulates when the reserve forces may be engaged, who may engage them, and further on the obligations, rights, and duties of the members of engaged reserve forces. It also prescribes the duties of the chief of the secretariat, this is on the second page of the document. So the chief, if I'm not mistaken, is responsible for planning the engagement of a specific number of forces in a method prescribed by this directive.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you see item 4 on your screen now?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment on that one.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Planning, organisation, coordination of the engagement of the reserve forces is carried out by the commander of the police station. When two or more members of the forces carried out -- carry out the tasks, the commander shall designate a patrol leader or a person in charge of the group or unit." So this is the subordination of the level of planning, organisation to the level of the commander of the police station since each police station had a certain number of the reserve forces that were available to them, that were deployed at that particular police station. So the commander of the police station could engage them, and he also had to define their tasks. This provision allows for the possibility that when two or more reserve forces personnel carry out duties, the commander can designate a patrol leader or the person in charge of that group. As far as I can remember, when regular duties were carried out, the patrol leader was always a member of the active force; such was the practice at the time. So the reserve forces member was in the patrol but we always insisted that active-duty police officers should be patrol leaders or should be those who decide on the way they will carry out their duties and authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Hannis, I just remembered that we received this document from the National Council for cooperation with the ICTY, and its origin is the archive of the Ministry of the Interior for 1998. Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Is the legal foundation for this document in the Law on the Ministry of the Interior, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is Article 7. Another thing that I would like to explain, Your Honours, the engagement of the reserve forces took place in 1998. This is what we heard on several occasions. I believe that we had the witness K89 for Suva Reka who was member of the reserve forces of the OUP Suva Reka. So the legal foundation was Article 7 of the Law on the Interior, and for the engagement of these forces in 1998 I will now ask to tender into evidence two additional documents, two orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And what it does essentially is authorise units of the ministry to engage reserve forces to carry out certain peacetime tasks of the ministry; is that the correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Article 37, 38, and 39, if I'm not mistaken, of the Law on the Ministry of the Interior describes the reserve forces and their engagement -- I believe in Article 37 their engagement at times of war; and Articles 38 and 39, the engagement of the reserve forces in peacetime. So the ministry has its reserve forces and the deployment and the status of these reserve forces are stipulated by law. I can find these specific provisions of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Djurdjic, my concern is what this document is doing, and it seems by paragraph 2 to be saying reserve forces may be engaged to carry out certain peacetime tasks of the ministry. And is that what this document is authorising?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, in 1998 the state of war was not declared in the Republic of Serbia. In 1998 terrorism as a criminal act was dealt by the -- as one of the regular tasks of the Ministry of the Interior. So the fight against terrorism at times of peace is a regular task of the Ministry of the Interior. And in 1998, if I'm not mistaken, it was Witness K89 who testified that he was member of the reserve forces -- of the reserve forces, and this was the basis for the engagement of reserve forces. And once you declare the state of war, then you have to apply another article of the Law of Internal Affairs, and I'm sorry I can't remember exactly which article it was, but it was used both by me and Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand that the events we're concerned with were events that occurred after a state of war had been declared; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is correct, Your Honour, but you can see how many witnesses and how much evidence we have relating to 1998 which indicate that things were carried out which were not in accordance with the regulations, and indeed the relevant period is between 1st of January and June 1999. But the Prosecution also tendered evidence related to the year 1998, so I believe this should not be controversial. But if you believe that various acts - and this is also an act issued pursuant to Article 7 of the Law of Internal Affairs - if you believe that we should not have any evidence pertaining to the year 1998, I will stop doing this; but I believe it is relevant for the period of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, it is your proposition that this is a document that regulated the use of reserve forces until such time as a declaration of war was made? And you would like us to receive it on that basis? Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no disagreement with that. We have argued that much of what happened in 1998 is relevant for your consideration of the final decision or judgement you're going to reach in this case. I did want to make a point, though, that Mr. Djurdjic made reference a couple of times to a witness he named as K89. I think it's K83 that he has in mind for this particular point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, are you satisfied, Mr. Hannis, in respect of that part of your objection which concerned the authenticity of the document in view of what Mr. Djurdjic has now been able to add?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes and no, Your Honour. If I may explain. If he received it from the National Council for Cooperation, most of the documents that we have tendered are documents we received that same way so we rely on them to be authentic, to be something that was retrieved from their archive pursuant to a specific request. However, I guess I still want to reserve the right to raise issues about the authenticity if there's something I see on the face of the document or the surrounding circumstances, and as I indicated I just had not seen one before where that entire portion of the document showing the assigned reference number for the document and the date, where that entire thing has been handwritten. Sometimes the number itself is handwritten and sometimes the date itself is handwritten, but the block usually will have date as typed, the word "date" or perhaps part of the year, and the number is typed to be filled in with a specific number. That's my only reservation, and I think I can argue from that later on. I just wanted to bring it to your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'll just observe, Mr. Hannis, that your experience is probably much greater than the experience I've had, but I have seen at times documents where there has been a rubber stamp applied which has blanks for then the insertion of the particular numbers and dates. And if you look closely at this document, you can see very, very faintly the possible presence of such a rubber stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I agree, Your Honour, I have seen that many times, sometimes at the top of the document, sometimes at the bottom where the signature block is. If there is a rubber stamp there then that makes me feel more comfortable about this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you would like us to receive this document, if that is our decision, subject to any -- your reservation and to any further information you may receive about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: On that basis, we receive the document, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00101, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If I could point out just another thing. We had problems with the dates of the documents from June, and all these dates were handwritten in the stamp and the same situation we have here on this one. Could I please now have the evidence D001-2920. This is yet another document that I received through the National Council for Cooperation. It again has a stamp and a reference number of the log-book handwritten in it. It is dated 1st of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, could you please tell me whether you're familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, is this the specific order on the basis of which, following the minister's decision, you can call-up and engage reserve forces to carry out these regular tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that in item 5 there is also the time-period that is designated for the engagement of such forces, between 1st of July and 31st of December, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00102, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask the court officer if we could have the document D001-2916.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The source of this document is the same; is that correct, Mr. Brakovic? Could you please read out item 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "According to this order, call-up and engage reserve forces personnel between 1st of January, 1999, and 30th of June, 1999."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this the foundation for the engagement of reserve forces to carry out regular tasks during the period indicated under item 5?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00103, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now kindly have document that is listed under 65 ter 01966.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, you stated your opinion about the format of this type of document, but I would like to hear one thing. We can see here that it's document Joint Command for KiM, Kosovo and Metohija, and we see the date here, and we see the strictly confidential number 45556; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please remember this -- this number. And then it also says strictly confidential and it's an order to rout and destroy the STS, Siptar terrorist forces, in the Malo Kosovo area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 5 in B/C/S and page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, who signed this order that we just saw?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Generally speaking, there is no signature here. It simply says the Joint Command for KiM. There is no usual signature, as one would expect. I expect there should have been a name, surname, the rank, and all the rest; and we can't see that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And just above that, what is written just above this Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean item 13?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, item 13, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Joint Command for KiM shall command -- direct all forces during combat operations from the Pristina area."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You graduated from the military academy, have you ever heard that there can be an order without the signature of the person issuing that order?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite honestly, I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could I now ask for this document to be tendered into evidence, or should I wait for yet another document that I would like to use?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As there is no objection, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00104, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would kindly ask the document listed under 65 ter, the number is 01967.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, once again can we see here the same formulation on the top of this document and could you please make sure that you pay attention to the number that is mentioned here. And also could you please focus on the title of the document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is amendment to the decision on supporting the MUP forces in breaking up and destroying STS in the area of Malo Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And on top of it we have the same reference number but also added slash 1, but otherwise the number is the same?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now please see the last -- the last page of the document. This is page 3 in B/C/S and page 5 in the English version or page 6. I'm not sure. Or page 3 in the English version. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, this amendment to the decision, is it signed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who signed it.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it is stated here, it is the commander Major-General Vladimir Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So, previously when we saw "Joint Command," could that actually be the commander of the Pristina Corps? And here again we have "Joint Command" on the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't really say who is behind that signature "Joint Command," but obviously it refers to the same order. This is amendment of the original order which was issued by Commander Vladimir Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So he amended that order as the commander of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the logic says that he was authorised to amend that order, so your conclusion may be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: As somebody with military background, could you explain to us how come that in one document we have Joint Command as the signatory without the proper signature and then later on in the amendment we have the commander of the unit who issued this order and the amendment of the order?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please explain? I haven't really understood your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you explain how come that the signatory of the first order was simply Joint Command and there was no signature of the commander in person who issued this order, and here in the amendment we have both the unit and the commander of that unit who issued this amendment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that question. I think that's calling on this witness to speculate. He is not a military officer. He doesn't know -- we have no evidence that he knows General Lazarevic or would know what he had in mind about signing one document and not signing another. If that's a point that Mr. Djurdjic wants to make, I'm willing to stipulate to the admission of parts of General Lazarevic's testimony in the MOS trial about this document and why he signed it and why he didn't sign the other one if he would like to have that, but I don't think it's appropriate for this witness to speculate on that point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness is a police general. He acted pursuant to the orders, and he explained that he always believed this to be a military document. Now I showed him a document to clarify who signed the amendment of the previous order, but I shall not insist on this any further. I will allow Your Honours to make your conclusions about this. I would just kindly ask this to be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00105, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now kindly ask the Defence document D001-2925.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, this is a decision of the Ministry of the Interior dated 19th July, 1998, on awards. Are you aware that the anti-terrorist unit members who were engaged in Kosovo were entitled to awards, and they indeed received the awards for merits in -- during them taking out their tasks?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that by this decision of 19th July 1998, the minister created the foundation for giving out such awards and prescribed the method whereby these awards would be issued?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that this is the first time that I see this document, but yes it follows from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you see item 5, Mr. Brakovic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: "Send the decision to the commands of the PJP, SAJ, and JSO units; the administration for joint affairs; and the headquarters of the ministry; and to the office of the ministry."

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So these were the addressees of this decision. Did you recommend your personnel for any awards?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm curious, is not this a general payment bonus for all people of the PJP and the SAJ and the JSO who were engaged in Kosovo and Metohija? You seem to be describing it as some special award or honour. Isn't this a pay document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, you're right. You're right. This is for the use -- I'm sorry. I made a mistake. Let me just say. Members of the active-duty PJP, once they're active, they are entitled to an increase in their salary. But when they are deployed in Kosovo and Metohija they received additional monetary awards in addition to their salaries, as is stipulated in this decision issued by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, is my interpretation of this document correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, in principle. So for each day of engagement in carrying out the tasks as specified here, there was an incentive payment to the amount of 50 dinars. I can't really now recall the value, but definitely this decision was complied with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And that's authorised by Article 40 of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. Well done, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's -- I'm merely reading the document. Don't think I have any great knowledge. I have much to learn about this. This document will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00106, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to ask the Court Deputy to put D001-3347 on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if you have the document. The only document that I see is the one in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told that there is no English translation in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Then I will merely have it marked for identification later.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right if I say that this is a document from the staff and the date is the 20th of October, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And that it was sent to the chiefs of the SUPs listed here and to the commanders of the orders of the PJP, SAJ, and JCO?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right that the subject of this document is the payment of 50 dinars per day, that is the bonus that we spoke about in -- well, could you please read the paragraph 1 of this document. That would be the best way.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to the decision of the minister of the payment of bonuses to the members of the PJP (active and reserve force) members of the SAJ and JCO for special merit in the execution of security tasks in suppressing terrorism in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, it is necessary to make lists for the periods between the 18th of September until the 17th of October, 1998," and then I think that in brackets it says "50 dinars per day."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Can you please read the next paragraph because it's fairly short.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Lists should contain information for the personnel who for justified reasons are not in the units and who are entitled to the bonus in accordance with to the criteria (wounded, sick, and et cetera)."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And could you please read the next passage slowly.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Requests for the appropriate amounts of money should be supplied by the commands of the detachments of the PJP, SAJ, and JCO to the OZZP of the secretariat by the 22nd of October, 1998, by 9.00 a.m. and the signed lists are to be submitted until the 23rd of October, 1998, and it is necessary to carry out the payment of the bonuses."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to have this marked for identification. I don't know if we need to submit an official translation after we've gotten this interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So can we learn who is the signatory, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, can you please tell us who -- could you please read the signature and the stamp.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Head of the staff Major-General Sreten Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please read everything, the stamp, what is handwritten over it.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the words "for"?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it means that somebody signed on his behalf, on the behalf of the head of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell us what is the number of this dispatch and the date? We have it in the heading.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please scroll down a little bit. Dispatch number 10-34 of the 20th of October, 1998, Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that now we have the whole document interpreted. Could I please be guided by you. Should I have it marked for identification or can we have it admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps we can identify who actually signed the document. It wasn't General Lukic; it was somebody signing purportedly for him. Is that recognised -- able to be recognised?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I really wouldn't like to go that far. I don't recognise the signature, as much as I would like to help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I perhaps jog the witness's memory? Because we have some more documents that bear the same signature. Your Honour, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... dangerously, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does this look like the signature of Mr. Mijatovic, who was the deputy of the head?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we perhaps zoom in on the signature, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it might well be since the first letter here is M, which indicates that it most probably is Mijatovic's signature, but again I can't really --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you can also see the stamp of the Ministry of the Interior; am I right?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if Mr. Hannis has any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, this will be marked for identification so that there can be a proper translation. Principally because of the uncertainty as to the signatory, it may become an issue at some later stage.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00107, MFI, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now I would like us to look at Defence document D002-4615.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, do you recognise the format of this document which was issued by the Pristina SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please read to yourself the document to familiarise yourself with its contents and then I would like to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would mention for the record that this is Exhibit D61 that's on the screen, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have any knowledge of it? And since we see that this pertains to the departure for Donje Obrinje of a team from the district court in Pristina, the deputy public prosecutor from the district office in Pristina who went there to carry out an exhumation - and I assume that your department provided an escort and general support. Are you familiar, therefore, with this thing?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the same document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is page 2 of the same document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 2 of this document in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please provide us with some more details based on your personal knowledge regarding this trip and the exhumation, when it was supposed to take place.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as I know and if I recall correctly, there was a request for an exhumation to be carried out in the village of Obrinje. I can see that an arrangement had been made for a team of pathologists with the investigation team involving the investigating judge, the deputy district public prosecutor was supposed to go there and the appropriate number of police officers was supposed to be assigned as their security. I took part in this activity, or rather, in a segment thereof because a certain number of police officers from the Pristina SUP was assigned to provide security, and I was in Glogovac. I had gone there to monitor this activity, to see it through to its end. I think, but I'm not 100 per cent sure, that Mr. Wolfgang Petritsch was also in the convoy. I'm not completely sure about that, but I think he was there too. And near a village, as you can see here, it says Trstenik, so it's only logical to assume that it was indeed there. The terrorists stopped the whole column and did not allow the police to go through, only the investigating judge was supposed to be allowed through, and the investigating judge did not want to go there. It was a lady. She didn't want to go there unaccompanied by the police. And I'm sure that this ended the whole exercise. The job was not done. Everybody went back to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So the contents of this document are accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I have document D003-0109.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document, Mr. Brakovic, to familiarise yourself, and then when I start asking questions we will proceed much faster.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, is this a memo from the MUP staff, number is 12A1098 and the date is the 3rd of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And is it signed by the head of the staff himself?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment on the first paragraph and tell us what you know about it.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first paragraph says that a certain number of persons who had participated in terrorist activities have been using false doctor's referrals for hospital treatment in order to escape more easily and safely from the territory where operations to mop-up terrorists are carried out and to enter towns.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You received this document and the commanders of the PJP detachments received it, therefore you got it too?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume that we did, although I can't really remember it with full certainty. But I am familiar with the contents of the document. I know that there were orders to that effect. Now, whether I received the orders to do so orally or whether I saw this document I really don't know, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00108, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I please have D003-0107.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, could you please look at the document and then I'm going to ask you some questions.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in a little bit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, is this document signed by the head of the staff?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the number is 12A9/98 and that the date is the 3rd of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 12A number?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: 12A number 9.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have 12A number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, in the heading.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see the heading.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You're reading the reference section.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, are you aware of what is stated here, there was this danger that some towns would perhaps be captured by the Siptar terrorist forces and that defence plans had to be drafted to cover for that eventuality?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know when Orahovac was actually attacked, whether it was before or after this memo. I assume that it happened before. The town itself was for all intents and purposes captured, and a lot of ethnic Serbs were abducted. So if it did happen -- if this did happen before, then probably this dispatch was the result of those events to prevent any such happenings. But many civilians were abducted. It was a regular occurrence in many places.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The Pristina SUP forwarded this dispatch to its organisational units, did it not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, yes. The dispatch is addressed to the chief. Now, whether he forwarded it or perhaps issued oral orders to that effect, I couldn't really tell you; but it doesn't really have any bearing on the essence of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00109, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, you mentioned Orahovac. It happened in July 1998, so one month before the document. But now I would like to ask you something about the -- an area that was not under your jurisdiction. Do you remember that in early July what the situation was like in the municipality of Pec and in Lodja? Do you have any knowledge of what the situation was like?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as regards the situation in the Secretariat of the Interior in Pec, I can give you in general terms that the situation was very serious; and as regards Lodja I know what the situation was like.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the KLA attacked a Serb house in early July and that there was fighting in Lodja, that police officers were kidnapped and that a fair number was injured?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know. I'm in fact quite familiar with the whole case since some of my friends were the casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right if I say that the police officers were captured or kidnapped and that they were later found and they were dead, they had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. They were the -- actually, an officer Srdjan Perovic from the Pec secretariat was abducted or captured, and the month later he was found -- his body was found and he was badly mutilated. I saw his autopsy pictures.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like us to look at D002-6440.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 6040.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, you are familiar with this format? These are reports from the forensic technicians from the crime scenes, and the date here is the 19th of August, 1998, and there is mention here of some photographs. Do you know anything about those facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at photographs 1 and 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, do you know that in Lodja members of the KLA set up fortifications and that after they pulled out of Lodja the fortifications were photographed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know about Lodja, but I did know that they -- that's what they did, those fortifications. I didn't go to Lodja myself, so I couldn't tell you that with full certainty, but all those places were fortified. There were fortifications built, and I have no reason to doubt that Lodja was an exception.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that it is time for our technical break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, apparently there is no English translation of this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we have the translation, but it was submitted -- did we submit it? Well, my associate tells me that it was submitted for translation but has yet to be translated. So if we could have it marked for identification, I would be very grateful; and then we can wait for the translation to be finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That, Your Honours, will be assigned D00110, MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, how is your time estimation with this witness, Mr. Djurdjic?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I believe that I will be done by the end of today. I will do my best to go as quickly as possible, but I do have a lot of area to cover, lots of documents to show to the witness, and documents that Mr. Hannis dealt with. I have two more documents that I would like to tender through this witness, and then I would like to move on to the documents that Mr. Hannis showed to him, and then I would also like to deal with some general issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would be desirable, Mr. Djurdjic, if you could finish today in time to allow Mr. Hannis to re-examine so that the witness doesn't carry over to yet another day. We leave you to try and plan your timing with that in mind. We have the first break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would kindly ask the document P356 to be displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, we are about to see a dispatch dated 18th of September, 1999 -- sorry, 18th of February, 1999. Could you agree with me that this dispatch was sent to chiefs of all the SUPs in the territory of Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you agree that it was also sent to the staff of the ministry for combatting terrorism in Pristina, bearing in mind the various authorities of that particular staff?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is written up here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that this dispatch was issued because of the realistic threat of the aggression by NATO on the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what is written in the beginning of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that the reasons for issuing this dispatch were timely preparation for defence against aggression, prevention of transfer of terrorist activities to other parts of the republic, atonement of the consequences of the aggression and normalisation of life?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what is written in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that no difference is made between the territory of Kosovo and Metohija -- SUPs in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, and the SUPs outside that territory?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed if this dispatch was sent to all the secretariats, then no difference is made.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that the Law on National Defence prescribes the roles and obligations of different elements in the defence of the republic and thus also the MUP had its plan for the defence of the entire Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I can assume but obviously this was not my narrow area of expertise but logic indicates that this would be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay, so you don't know this. But am I right to say that all the SUPs in the territory of the republic had to have their defence plans and thus also the Pristina SUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that in the police administration of MUP in the PJP department there was a section for the preparation of defence plans?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that the police department of the Pristina SUP in the territory of its secretariat directly organises and prepares defence activities of the secretariat in case of an imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it issues measures to other organisational units.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that your department had to establish the set-up of various organisational units in case of an imminent threat of war?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, one could say so pursuant to a request issued by commander of police station as we could see previously in various orders, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that within your department when it comes to the defence plan of Pristina SUP, there is a plan of measure for readiness and the plan for defence preparation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there should have been one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that in your police department this particular task was carried out by the inspector for police defence plans and reserve forces?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was an officer for that particular task to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right to say that this officer carried out these tasks as one part of his regular tasks and duties?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among other things.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that pursuant to the Law on Internal Affairs, Article 27, it is prescribed that the Ministry of the Interior in case of an imminent threat of war could use military conscripts?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the first part of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That the Ministry of the Interior for its activities in case of an imminent threat of war or war could be staffed by military conscripts deployed as reserve forces of MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that in the SUP units there were never no volunteers and that only military forces following its procedure could take on volunteers in its units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only talk about MUP. We did not receive any volunteers. Whether the military received volunteers and following which procedure, probably yes, but I couldn't talk about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we show item 7 of this document of this decision. This is on page 2 of the B/C/S version and I believe page 3 -- yes, page 3 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is this item an instruction for the operational work to identify and put under control units of volunteers in order to prevent their activities?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we kindly have the evidence P133, the Exhibit P133 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, this is a dispatch dated 28th of July, 1998. Am I right to say that this was again sent to all the SUPs in the territory of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this was sent to all the commands of the PJP -- of the PJP detachments?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this dispatch was also sent to the Pristina command?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is also written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that pursuant to the decision on training of special police units following a -- authority of the -- or authorisation by the minister, the chief of department could make decisions on the engagement of PJP units?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not the most competent person to provide legal interpretation of different provisions of the decision, but I -- in my mind you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, I'm not asking for any interpretation, but I'm just wondering what is your knowledge concerning the application of police legislation, legislation related to the police, particularly in view of the fact that you were a police general and also that you have military background, that you graduated from the military academy, but obviously it is only up to the Court to provide legal interpretation. Am I right to say that this dispatch does not determine any task which units ...

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see on the first page of this dispatch, this is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now have a look at the second page of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that on the second page also this is not the case?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right to say that all the logistics concerning transportation, payment of per diems, provision of meals was supposed to be carried out by a general affairs unit? This was on the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was always the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, you mentioned in the transcript of the 8th of May on page 4159, lines 3 to 8, that in the activities of 124 Intervention Brigade for the year 1998/1999 the focus of this report was -- so the focus of the report was the equipment, armament, and numbers of forces and not so much the activities. Am I right that this report was submitted by you when the MUP staff for combatting terrorism ceased to be in operation?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at the time-line, this should have been the case, given that I compiled this report possibly in September - I can't say that for sure. And the staff should have ceased to be in operation after the 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When asked by Mr. Hannis, you said that KLA used to wear military uniforms on different occasions or police uniforms. This is something that you stated on 7th of May, transcript page 4129, page [as interpreted] 25, and page 4130, lines 1 to 3. Am I right to say that they also put different coloured bands on their arms in order to distinguish themselves?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this was the purpose of them wearing the different colour bands on their arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now see the exhibit from the list 65 ter number 0321.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, these are the minutes from the meeting of the staff on the 27th/28th of July, 1998. I assume that Mr. Hannis failed to show this -- this was an oversight since he tendered all the other minutes into the -- into evidence and they have indeed been admitted. That's P688, that's what my associate tells me, but I don't think so. I don't have it. I only have the 65 ter number listed here, and I'm sure that Mr. Hannis did not exhibit this. That's the 29th of July and the meeting was held on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like Mr. Hannis to correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I did not use that document, Your Honour, and I don't know when it got exhibit number 688 but that was before I appeared.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- it was not used by Mr. Hannis. Do you want to ask something about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, just very briefly. I thought it was not admitted into evidence, and that's why I wanted -- well, the format is okay and if it has indeed been admitted -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You did not attend this meeting, but I'm interested in page 7 in the English version. It's paragraph -- it's the second paragraph from the bottom which would be page 6 in the Serbian version. Mr. Brakovic, the chief of the SUP of Pristina, Bosko Petric, attended this meeting. Now, I would like you to comment on what he says. "The Belacevac is being secured by us" and he makes the following comment: "Without us there wouldn't be anything ..." What was the situation like there? Could you please give us some more details.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could I please have it in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would be page 6 in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, on the basis of what the secretariat chief said, I can only assume that he was referring to the open mine in Belacevac which supplied thermo-electric plants Kosovo A and Kosovo B that would generate power using that coal. As far as I know, that coal-mine was in the hands of the KLA for a while. And then we had one or two actions that were launched in order to have it operational again because the power supply of the country was at stake. At least that's how it was presented on TV. So I assume that this was the case. I know that a certain number of our people was used to secure this open-pit coal-mine, and I think that was it more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me whether this coal-mine had been taken by the KLA at any point in 1998 and did you take any measures in this regard, you as the police department or as the intervention brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I've just answered your question. It was under their control. Some of the employees had been abducted. It was controlled by the KLA, and then we launched one or two actions - I think two actions - and we were able to put Belacevac coal-mine under our control again. It has two parts. And then the power generation went on as usual. And as I said, we provided partial security to it afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not sure if this 65 ter document has already been admitted. It's 04153 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P688.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could I please then have 688.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's what you just had on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, I would like to have a new 65 ter document. I can see that there was a bar table motion for the admission of all those documents, but these are the conclusions. I wasn't aware of this bar table motion. All right. My associate will give me the exhibit number, but let us start asking questions and then we'll deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, these are the conclusions from the meeting held on the 7th and 11th of May, 1999, at the MUP staff. You were not there on the 7th when all the chiefs were, but you were there on the 11th of May, 1999, and you did confirm that. Now I would like you to look at paragraph 1. Do you recall that you were told about the contents of the communique that was -- from the meeting that was held in the office of the President of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, Slobodan Milosevic, and this was actually forwarded to everyone -- in fact, it was a press release that was published in Politika and a press clipping was attached to it.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have to say that I'm not sure whether I saw that in that period, but I know that I saw it in the course of the proofing for my evidence in a document somewhere. But at any rate, I'm not sure that I actually recall it -- having seen it in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And do you know that the head of the staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija together with the commander of the 3rd Army actually submitted a report to the supreme commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw that in a document as I was being proofed for my evidence here. I can't really remember whether I saw it at that time, whether I have any recollection of it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, as regards item 7, do you remember if you took any measures to prevent any movements of civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the secretariat took measures because I was in the field a lot, so I can't really give you any credible account of that. I'm not really competent to talk about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, please do tell us only things you know about. Now, as regards paragraph 11 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move on to the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you take any measures regarding paragraph 11; and if yes, what measures?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ensure that members of the police carry out all their assigned tasks lawfully and so on, absolutely yes -- in fact, we instituted criminal and disciplinary proceedings against some of our personnel for some minor crimes, theft, things like that. I can give you an example that stuck in my memory: A police officer stole 15 kilos of washing powder and disciplinary proceedings were instituted against him. I don't know whether he was criminally prosecuted too, but I do know that he was disciplined and he was suspended from duty although he was an excellent policeman -- well, professionally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understand it is already an exhibit, Exhibit P688.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My mistake. We'll receive it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document under 65 ter 04153, Your Honours, will be assigned D00111.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have Exhibit P768.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, this -- these are the minutes from the meeting of the MUP staff. The date is the 22nd of July, 1998. The meeting was held in Pristina. And now I would like to ask you if this meeting in the staff followed immediately after the KLA took Orahovac and the police forces then liberated it immediately after that. I think it was on the 19th of July.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Am I right when I say that the assistant ministers, Generals Djordjevic and Stevanovic, attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
