utterances.text: And am I right that the minister of the interior decided whom and when to send on any kind of business trip?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that, but I can only assume that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that the assistant ministers of the interior on the one hand relay the orders of the minister and on the other report to the minister about the situation in the field or report from the meetings --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic, the witness doesn't know this in so many things of his own knowledge. You're really asking him either just to read the document and repeat what is in it or to conjecture as to what happened because of it or what caused it. It's really not advancing the case at all. We can read the document and see what's in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please comment, if you can, on the intervention of the Pristina SUP chief Bosko Petric who said that the situation in the territory covered by the Pristina SUP was very difficult. Could you please tell us in detail what the situation was and why was it described as difficult, in what respect.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is quite difficult to me to do so because you could see on Friday when I was asked similar questions by the Prosecution to recall all those things that were said at the meeting --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not -- let me interrupt you. I'm not asking you what he said. I'm asking you what you knew about the situation covered -- situation in the territory covered by the Pristina SUP in that time-period. This was merely a pretext for me to ask you that, if you remember; if you don't remember, fair enough.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I'm not mistaken, at the time Glogovac was the most problematic area because the road leading from Glogovac to Srbica was cut and could not be used and there were quite a few attacks in the area between Glogovac and Komorane. That was a place on the road between Pristina and Pec, and in general in the Glogovac area there were quite a few locations that were not controlled by the army and the police, they were controlled by the KLA. As far as Podujevo was concerned, the situation there was better, substantially better. There were some locations that were also controlled by the KLA. And now as regards Obilic, probably that area in the direction of Cicavica, it is a mountain of sorts, and the Drenica area, Lipljan, it was also controlled by the KLA in that period if my memory serves me right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have to say that I was quite astonished when

utterances.speaker: MR. PETRIC SAYS
utterances.text: "The situation in the town of Pristina, the security situation is quite favourable. We had only two explosions." What was the situation like when the situation was not favourable? How many explosions did you have then?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't say that because ten years have passed, but I can tell you that in the town of Pristina itself we dealt with classical acts of terrorism. There were attacks, explosive devices that were set in various buildings, vehicles used by various persons. So there were quite a few attacks on police personnel in the town itself or in the villages around Pristina, the outskirts of Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, when I put something to you, I'm not asking you to comment or interpret the words of the person saying it; I'm just asking you what you know about that topic. So I don't want you to go and read what it says in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have P769 up on our screens.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, these are the minutes of the meeting held on the 26th of October, 1998. It's the MUP staff meeting. And I would like to look at paragraph 13. That's at page 2 of the English version. So paragraph 13, this is on page 2 of the B/C/S and English version. My question for you, Mr. Brakovic, is as follows: Given that nearly -- you spent nearly all your career in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, do you remember at which time the reserve police departments were set up and whether it was in any way linked to the events that occurred in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reserve police departments, I believe that they were set up in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So before 1998 there were no reserve police departments?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, RPOs or reserve police departments did not exist prior to 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In these minutes we can see the numbers of the reduced police forces in Kosovo and Metohija in relation to the agreement, but this is not my question. My question is whether the reorganisation of the units of the approved police units could be done by the staff after the signing of the verification agreement. So could it be done by the staff, the planning, deployment of the police forces in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean of the forces that were in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, of the approved number of forces that were there in accordance with the verified agreement.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume so, though this was not my area of responsibility, but I would assume so. There was a number of check-points along the routes, along the roads, which I believe defined together with first of all KDOM mission and then OMS mission, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, were you personally aware of the agreement, the agreement of the October and Kosovo Verification Mission, do you remember that you read this agreement?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that now. I probably did, but I really can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From that period between October and the beginning of the war, do you know what were the relations of the verifiers and verifying commission with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any direct knowledge, but there were some comments that -- saying that the verifiers were lenient towards KLA, that in a way assisted them by providing them some information and so on, but I had no direct knowledge about this because I was not involved in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you receiving any intelligence either from the area of public security or state security?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not. Possibly the chief of the secretariat received such intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the Exhibit P690, yes, P690.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, I would like to know -- paragraph 5 of this document, could you maybe provide your comments? What is it all about?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is stated here that it was necessary to submit to the verification mission information on armed villages with estimates of the amount of weapons that they have. And from the continuation of the text I can conclude that they're probably thinking about Albanian armed villages, and so it should be requested that they disarm them and inform them that if they do not do it the police will have to do it but they will not take responsibility for the consequences and also submit the information around the villages to the staff by 1500 hours on the 6th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Are we talking about illegal holding of weapons, illegal holding of unpermitted weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please take a look at paragraph 10 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, am I right to say that in this paragraph the units, the PJP units, sent are different from the units that are in the territory of Kosovo; and by this paragraph the staff actually orders to the units sent --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're talking about paragraph 10?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes. So you as the detachment 124, you continued carrying out your regular job, for example, you yourself as chief of the police in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right to say that this paragraph 10 shows that the staff is sending the PJP units and putting them under Kosovo SUP's, and you coming from the 124th Brigade, so you were not sent especially on this occasion, you actually would just return to carry out your regular tasks, in your particular case the tasks of the chief police in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read out this paragraph 10 this is certainly the conclusion that you can draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we just clarify yet another thing. A formations are usually manoeuvre units, whereas B formations are territorial units which control the territory? And if we have R then these are reserve forces; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see the Exhibit P770.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the intervention of President Milutinovic. Could you agree with me that in the given period the intention was to use political means to resolve the Kosovo problem and that this was also suggested as the official state policy to you within the police at the time? So what was your reading of this particular speech by Mr. Milutinovic, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember details from this speech. I should read this out.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Then it's quite okay. We shall proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the Exhibit P689, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: This is dated 2nd of December, 1998. Could you please comment --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is page 3 in the English version and in B/C/S it is on page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I can see that Mr. Bozidar Filic as a representative of the Pristina SUP attended this meeting and his comment was the security situation in the territory of Pristina SUP was more complex and more difficult, and particularly in the territory of Malisevo, Glogovac, and Podujevo. Could you recall what was the situation like and why was it described at the time in this particular way?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that after the signing of the Milosevic-Holbrooke Agreement, the KLA was revitalised so to say and we had problems controlling certain territories. Given that we held the road leading to Malisevo, I remember that there were quite a few attacks there and I believe that at the time two police officers were kidnapped and later killed. In the territory of Podujevo, towards the end of 1998 and in early 1999, started to be a security issue which -- and this was not the case earlier, but at that time they already started building as you described fortifications, or rather, trenches, and they kept certain territory under their control. So this is in brief a description of the situation. Possibly I could go into further details, but I also forgot quite a lot in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, are you familiar with the fact that after the signing of the verification agreement and after the withdrawal of the military forces and the police forces from certain areas, that these areas were then re-occupied by the forces of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, when it comes to arming and training of the members of the KLA after the signing of the agreement, do you know anything about that during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were comments that the logistics, and training, equipping of their forces were underway, but I have no direct knowledge about this. I only have second-hand information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Is that the information that you received during the meetings held at the staff?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, among other sources I also heard them at the meetings held at the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you were present in these meetings and you heard yourself what is then also recorded in the minutes?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have the Exhibit P85.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, these are the minutes dated 17th of February, 1999. In B/C/S could you kindly take this page up so that we comment on something that Mr. Hannis already asked you about. Mr. Brakovic, General Lukic - this is in a context of his intervention - talks about plan activities in the event of an attack. Am I right to say that all this was within the framework of the defence plan of a possible NATO attack, NATO aggression, if it was to happen?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please take this page up a bit more. In the first part here it is stated that there is an elaborated plan in order to prevent the possible entry of military forces of the NATO pact to our territory, if this is your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, and this is a part of the general plan.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, but I can only assume that this is a part of a general plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You can see here the numbers of units of various kinds. Am I right when I say that this 900 are 900 members of the reserve forces of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it is written here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So these are policemen that are planned for -- these are policemen that are in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that for sure, but I can assume that this is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please now have the Exhibit 764.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting for this exhibit, Mr. Brakovic, how were you notified that you should attend the meeting in the ministry, or rather, at the staff of the ministry?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably I was told by the chief, or somebody would call me on the phone and tell me that I should attend the meeting at such and such time.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now we have the minutes of the 4th of April, 1999. Do you remember where did you attend this meeting, where was this meeting held?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you. I think that on one occasion I was in the Chamber of Commerce and on another occasion it was the Executive Council building or maybe it was on the both occasions. I really can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In the minutes here, Lieutenant-General Obrad Stevanovic is recorded as being present. Now I would like to ask you something about General Stojanovic, or rather, Stevanovic. In Pristina in 1998 and 1999, was there a PJP command?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, it did not exist. There was the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And your detachment, or rather, your PJP brigade, what was its strength?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I've already answered the most approximate figure would be about 950. I think the top limit would be about 1.000.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You didn't hear my question. The question was the command of the 124th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the number of people in the command was very, very small, not more than ten, seven, eight people approximately were there including the store men and the logistics people. So seven to eight people.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right that the assistant head of the staff from June 1998 for the PJP was Goran Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I saw that the decision to set up the staff specified that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In 1999 and 1998 while you attended the staff meetings, did you ever hear anyone say that they were the commander of a PJP unit and that they reported to the staff on any issue, that they briefed the staff?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if my memory serves me right, I don't think that was the case. It was a long time ago, but I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 3 of the English version, the second bullet point from the bottom. I'm interested in this part -- in the Serbian version that would be page 3 as well or maybe page 4. This entry where it says: "Take rigorous measures if any paramilitary units appear there."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about measures taken and what you yourself had to do, if you have any knowledge?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory covered by the Pristina SUP, I did not have any knowledge of the existence of any paramilitary units. So that would be more or less my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'm interested in page 6 in the English version, the bullet point I want you to look at is the second one. The exchange of intelligence data between the RJB and RDB, that for that purpose you had to talk to the staff. Did you have any problems, any specific problems, and did you exchange information?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What bullet point is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's page 4, bullet point 2, if there are any problems -- that's bullet point 3 on page 6 of the English version, if there are any problems regarding the exchange of information between the RJB and RDB please report so those problems could be resolved. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't been able to find anything here. Now, as regards the exchange of information -- well, this was probably done by the chief of the secretariat, so I did not have a lot of information about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, it's page 3 in the Serbian version -- well, we've dealt with that. Thank you. Well, I don't have any questions pertaining to this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I now have P345, page 5, please, in the B/C/S version and let me give you a page reference for the English version. I'm interested in paragraph 13, or rather, paragraph 12. That's page 6 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, as regards the words of Mr. Colic, who was the commander of the Djakovica company in your brigade regarding the reservists, am I right that crimes committed by military personnel were prosecuted by the military police?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the civilian police can only respond if they come across a perpetrator in the course of the perpetration of the crime and then they can arrest this perpetrator and hand him over to military organs?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that Commander Colic on this occasion briefed the staff that SUP Djakovica informed the relevant military authorities about all those incidents?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Am I right then that the Djakovica SUP, or rather, he himself acted in accordance with the law and that he could not take any other measures?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 7 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move to page 7. It's in the Serbian version. That's page 8 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please tell me in the first paragraph of the conclusions the head of the staff says: "Massive moving out of the civilians should be prevented as soon as possible ..." What was this all about, Mr. Brakovic, could you tell us? Do you recall any specific examples from that period and what you did in that regard?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of what I can see in the minutes, this pertained more to the sphere of the regular general-duty police within the secretariat. I couldn't really comment on it. I remember that measures were ordered to put a stop to it and that the police should be dispatched to go there to tell the citizens that there is no reason for them to move out, but I really can't recall any details because as I said this was done by the general-duty regular police more than we did. It was not among our tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, the indictment alleges that from the 24th of March until the end of May, 1999, that the FRY and Serbian forces went into the houses of Albanians in Pristina, forcing the inhabitants to leave. You as the commander of the police department, or rather, chief of the police department, I do apologise, do you have any knowledge of that, and could you tell us something about the situation in the town of Pristina in the period following the 24th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have any knowledge of that because in that period I had other tasks that were the problem that I had to deal with. It was a war. We had people deployed at Bukovo Glava, a repeater that was completely encircled by the KLA, and we had to plan their evacuation. We had to do it as soon as possible. And even in normal conditions the facility could be reached only by helicopter and it was not possible at the time. So this was a problem that we had to deal with. Secondly, as is well-known, there were a massive air-strikes by NATO aeroplanes targeting all MUP facilities because there were many such facilities in Pristina including various depots. So all this had to be organised to protect and shelter the personnel, and this included also the secretariat building in Pristina. It was hit on the 29th of March. There was also the problem of communication with Malisevo, or rather, the road to Malisevo. The secretariat personnel had to secure it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... the question was: Did you have knowledge of a particular issue? You said in your first sentence that you didn't. And you've now gone on very extensively saying what else you were doing. That's not going to -- we have some interference in the sound system. It's cleared from my phones now. All of this is just irrelevant, Mr. Djurdjic. Is there something you want that is of use to us from this witness about this document or any other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, did you ever receive any orders or did you ever issue any orders from the Albanian civilians to be expelled and evicted from their homes in Pristina and to force them to leave?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge that police and military forces killed Albanian civilians in the town of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't have any knowledge of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you receive or issue any orders that at each intersection in Pristina Albanian civilians should be directed towards buses and trains so that they could be transported to Albania and Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you receive or issue any orders for Kosovo civilians to be stripped of their personal documents, their ID cards at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know of any orders that were issued or any such goings-on in the villages in the municipality of Pristina in terms of expulsions and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you issue any orders or did you tolerate if there was any information to the effect that the police were abusing Albanian civilians, in particular any sexual assaults against women?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any knowledge of that because if I had had any knowledge I would have taken appropriate measures as stipulated by the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Precisely, or rather, thank you. Did you have any knowledge or did you issue any orders to the police forces under your command to destroy cultural heritage, places of worship belonging to Muslims, or businesses?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Brakovic, since the indictment alleges that there was a pattern of conduct according to which the forces of the FRY and the Republic of Serbia would always surround villages and towns inhabited by Albanian civilians in Kosovo and Metohija and then proceeded first to shell those habitations and then went in, looted, and destroyed the buildings and that there never was any fighting, first of all, did you ever shell any Albanian villages or villages where there were civilians without any fighting?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that it was a 100 per cent certainty. I might be wrong to a small extent, but in all anti-terrorist actions that I took part in, there were no civilians in the inhabited areas where those -- where the fighting went on. So the population had been evacuated, I assume by the KLA, prior to any fighting, so that at this time I cannot recall a single location where anything of the sort happened, where we would come across towns or villages where there still were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I would now like to know this: Did it ever happen to you, because there were civilians in those inhabited areas, that you did not proceed with your actions because of the presence of the civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I provided you with part of my answer in my previous answer. I don't think that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did it ever happen in Kosovo and Metohija that KLA members used places of worships and schooling as firing positions and offered resistance from those facilities?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that this did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, after the war, you were transferred to Niska Banja, I mean the SUP, the Pristina SUP was relocated there?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether Albanian civilians went there and applied for passports and all the other documents and actually got them, just as they had before the 1999 war?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, I saw that. But of course I didn't deal with that, but I could see civilians come in and seeking to exercise their basic rights, applying for documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Am I right that the registers of births and so on and other register books such as the register of citizens, that they were all preserved and that all citizens of Serbia are able to exercise their right to have those documents as usual and that they can always get it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume that they have been preserved. I can't really tell you that with 100 per cent certainty, but I assume that they were because I didn't hear of any problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If somebody loses a passport or an ID card, does that mean that somebody can lose his own identity?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, are you aware that the practice of the members of the KLA after their withdrawal from villages was to go to the woods and take civilian population with them?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know about the practice of the members of the KLA, that once they withdrew from villages they would go to the woods and they would take the civilian population with them to use them for protection?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said that in all the activities in which I took part in various inhabited areas on a number of occasions we came across groups of civilians away from those inhabited areas. So certainly KLA used them, and also they changed their clothes into civilian clothes and used groups of civilians in order to move along with them, so to disguise them among the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Brakovic, did your department provide protection to Mr. Rugova during the war in 1999, during his stay in Pristina? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not my department. It was the police, so police officers, a certain number of police officers provided security for Mr. Rugova in his house in Pristina. I can't remember how many, but this is certainly the case. Possibly it would be interesting to mention that there was an attempted assault against Mr. Rugova by an Albanian, and I remember this very well because I was there during the investigation. This Albanian had a blue vest, and I remember that he tried to assault him with one single pistol. He was supposed to cross a fence at a place wherefrom he could enter the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us whether in March in 1999 at the beginning of the war there was an attack on the police station in the quarter of Vranjevac in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember that now. It is possible even probable, but I cannot remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the old market is in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The old market-place, I know where the new market is located. I thought it was the only one. Maybe you can help me out with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I can't. If you don't know where it is, you don't.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know where new market is. This is in the settlement of Vranjevac, near the TV station, Pristina TV station building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: From that position, can you see the top of the Vranjevac hill?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not 100 per cent certain but you can see quite a lot from there. There was also a small market in Pristina, so I haven't forgotten all my basics. I'm just not sure of that name, "the old market."

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether military forces or police forces shelled the part of the town Kojlovac in March 1999? Do you remember any shelling at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The quarter called Kojlovica, I don't know that precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there -- was there any combat against KLA forces in the town of Pristina itself in the beginning of the war, maybe in March?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly there were some small skirmishes but there was no serious conflict, military conflict in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were there check-points in the town of Pristina?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Were all the persons crossing these check-points controlled regardless of their nationality in order to prevent any infiltration by the KLA members?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So there was no discrimination on the grounds of nationality?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the entry point of the town of Pristina, were all the persons and vehicles entering the town checked regardless of their nationality?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, I need to say that the purpose of these check-points was more to prevent possible theft of vehicles and other items. This is as much as I can remember now. This was the focus of our attention because there were incidents of car thefts. So in order to prevent that, in order to prevent these vehicles being taken away from the town, we had to check all of them in order to make sure that the real owners of the vehicles were the persons driving them. So this was the focus of our activities without now going at length.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Brakovic. I have a lot of other questions for you, but I appreciate the wish stated by the Trial Chamber that you should be able to leave The Hague today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honours, I believe it may be time for a break although I know that Mr. Hannis also probably has some questions for Mr. Brakovic. And if you can allow me before we do that my assistant has just pointed out that MFI 907 has been translated and could we see whether it could be tendered into evidence now -- or actually, it has already been admitted into evidence as Exhibit 107 so there is no need to do that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I just confirm, Mr. Djurdjic, you've completed your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The court officer will tell me in a moment whether we have any problem with that exhibit that you have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There will be an order admitting the translation into the exhibit, and it will -- the document marked for identification will now become an exhibit with the same number. We will now have the second break, and we resume at 1.00, Mr. Hannis. Thank you, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, one of the exhibits that you saw had to do with the composition of the MUP staff for suppression of terrorism that was created by the minister in June of 1998. And Mr. Djurdjic asked you yesterday about David Gajic and you indicated you understood that David Gajic worked in the state security department; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General Djordjevic, as the assistant minister and as the head of public security, would he have any authority to appoint a member of state security to any kind of position?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, could you kindly repeat your question? I mistakenly changed the language of my earphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: As I understand the organisation in the MUP, the two primary divisions were between public security, which was headed by General Djordjevic in 1998, and state security, which in the first part of 1998 was headed by Jovica Stanisic. General Djordjevic, as head of public security, did he have the ability to appoint or name somebody like David Gajic in state security to a position on the MUP staff or not?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were shown another document and asked about the appointment of Major-General Momcilo Stojanovic to the MUP staff in Pristina in 1998. Do you know what his position was with the MUP staff? What was his job?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, he dealt with certain issues pertaining to housing provision. I believe this is what I saw in the decision appointing him as member of the staff. Possibly if we could see this document I could answer with more precision, but I'm certain that he dealt with that because I was personally interested in resolving my housing situation. So I personally seeked information from him on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. No, that's sufficient. I'm going to try really hard to finish so that you can go home today. Let me move on to Exhibit P57. Again, this is that decision to establish a MUP staff for suppression of terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have that on the screen, and I need the bottom of page 1 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's tab 26 in your binder if you want to look at the hard copy. And I think we probably have to go to page 2 in the B/C/S. It's item number 2 that talks about the staff's task, and it says: "The staff's task is to plan, organise, and control the work and engagement of organisational units of the ministry and also sent and attached units in suppressing terrorism in the autonomous province of Kosovo ..." Would all the PJP units that were in Kosovo in 1998 and later on in 1999 fall under this definition?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. Here it is stated "sent and attached units."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. As I understand it PJP units were not organisational units as defined in the MUP rules; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The organisational units in the sense of their permanent functioning, they were not such units; that's correct. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And your 124th Brigade under this -- this paragraph would be an attached unit?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't define it in legal terms. It was not a sent unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- so I assume that secretariats and the 124th Intervention Brigade were in the same context. Possibly legally they could be described as attached units, but I couldn't really state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you about -- yesterday you were asked a question about your job as commander of the 124th, and Mr. Djurdjic asked you at page -- transcript page 4212, line 14: "Q. And while you did the job of the commander, you did not submit reports to the SUP chief?" Your answer was: "A. I did not." You went on to say, Except unfortunately if there were any injuries or casualties of any sort. You did that, but you called that informing or notification not reporting. Can you answer this question for me: Who were you reporting to when doing your PJP work if it was not the SUP chief, either in the SUP or higher up in the MUP that you reported to?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When it comes to the tasks of the 124th Intervention Brigade, as I said these were the tasks related to anti-terrorist activities and the reports concerning such activities, generally speaking, were sent by the operational head of a particular task. This was usually a military officer. And the information was provided to the secretariat, so if there were any casualties, any injuries inflicted, I was obliged to inform urgently the secretariat concerning such an event.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you report to -- did you personally as brigade commander report to or inform anybody in the MUP besides the SUP chief about PJP activities and other matters relating to your PJP work?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Djurdjic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has just said that he did not inform the SUP chief when he was appointed the commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade. This may have been an error made by Mr. Hannis because the witness stated the opposite, that when he was working as the commander of the 124th Brigade he did not inform or he did not report to the SUP chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's not the way I read the particular answer. It's merely given as usually and particular tasks. So carry on, Mr. Hannis, and try and clear up this matter if you could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: First of all, I understood yesterday when you were answering questions about that, that you drew a distinction between reporting and informing. Am I right about that, that in your mind there is a difference between those two things?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there is a distinction, and if necessary I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you do that very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reporting, submitting reports, this is a combat document whereby an officer informs the superior command, the command that issued an order or task about the situation and intentions in relation to that tasks -- to that task. So this is an activity that is very strictly stipulated in terms of hierarchy. Provision of information is provision of information concerning a certain fact, and you can inform somebody who is your superior or your subordinate or somebody of the same rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I hope you can understand this. So when I'm informing somebody about something, I can also inform a colleague of mine who is my peer in order to supply him with information about certain events, certain activities, so that he may avoid having the same problems. But when I submit report, this is very strictly defined activity, and I try to explain how that functioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand from your answer it sounds like reports were only written. Were there no oral reports?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I indicated who submitted written reports. Now, as for the oral reports, I think that I've already explained that the MUP staff would receive oral information when they called us up and asked us about the situation in the field, and we also informed them about any relevant issues, casualties, and so on, and everything that had to do with the secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In 1998 and 1999 in connection with your role as commander of the 124th Intervention Brigade, did you report to or inform anybody other than the SUP chief in Pristina, your peers, or MUP staff about the activities of your brigade, anybody higher, anybody in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. One of the early questions you got today related to your job as head of the police department in Pristina. Mr. Djurdjic asked you if you were supposed to be notified of visits by the minister of the interior, deputy ministers, and other officials who would come to the territory covered by Pristina SUP. Your answer at page 4, line 11 was: "A. Well, yes, the logic dictated that I should be notified." I agree, logic dictates, but did the rules or procedure require that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you how it is. When the minister comes, the security measures are stepped up; and since I was directly in charge of that, that's how I said it, the logic dictated that, yes, I should be notified in order to be able to take appropriate measures, to make the minister stay and the stay of everybody else as safe and as pleasant as possible because it didn't mean that they should be safe only in the building but they were supposed to travel somehow. So throughout the territory covered by the secretariat that I belonged to, it was my task to draft the plan, the security plan, and the routes that they would take, and this is why I gave the answer that I gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. How would you receive such notification? Was it in writing or orally; and if so, from whom did you receive it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I usually would receive it from the chief of the secretariat as a rule. It was almost always the rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know who he received the information from?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you. He may have received it from one of the staffs or possibly he received the information about the visits of high-ranking officials, including ministers, by a dispatch, and then appropriate measures, security and safety measures, had to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I appreciate your efforts to be helpful; but if you don't know, it's okay to say you don't know. Let me ask you: Did it always happen that you got notification in 1998 and 1999 when the minister or the assistant ministers, including General Djordjevic, when they came to visit Pristina? Or were there times when you discovered later that they had come for a visit and you had not been notified?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I was notified, except in cases where -- when I was in the field and then I would learn of that subsequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you receive notice that General Djordjevic was in Pristina on or about the 1st of June, 1999, and attending a meeting with Mr. Sainovic, General Pavkovic, General Lukic, and Mr. Andjelkovic, among others?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is the first time that I hear of something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to ask you about instructions. At page 5, line 10, today you were asked about instructive dispatches and whether or not they had the force of an order. General -- Mr. Djurdjic asked you if those instructive dispatches tell people how to do something and not so much what to do. Your answer was at line 17: "A. Well, one could say that." Did those instructions have to be obeyed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please ask me a specific question. Instructions as to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the original question from Mr. Djurdjic was in the context of an instruction on how tasks should be implemented and carried out, for example. Did those kind of instructions have to be obeyed?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes at any rate in accordance with the law, regulations, and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: What consequences, if any, would flow from a failure to follow an instructive dispatch?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, everything depends on the consequences thereof, cautions or reprimands, and even some disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Do you know where in the rules for the Ministry of the Interior is there a definition of instructive dispatches that distinguishes them from something more onerous like a directive or an order? Can you tell us where we might find that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't really tell you at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You were shown today at page 10, line 17, an exhibit that was marked D101. This was, I think, a directive dated the 22nd of June, 1998, and this was the one that dealt with how the reserve forces were engaged. Do you remember that one?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instruction on the performance of internal affairs duties of persons from the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know whether that directive was ever modified or withdrawn or superseded by a later directive after 22 June 1998 and some time before June of 1999? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I don't think so. But let me stress once again I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Exhibit D106 that you were shown today, and this is the one that talked about extra pay or supplemental pay bonus for those PJP, SAJ, and JSO personnel who were dispatched to engage in Kosovo after July 18th or 19th, 1998. And you'll see a reference in paragraph 2 to "... the commands of the PJP, SAJ, and JSO units ..." Can you tell me what that refers to? Is that -- are those some body -- some organs in the ministry or is that at your level? I'm not sure of what "... commands of the PJP, SAJ, and JSO ..." means in that context.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: " ... PJP, SAJ, and JSO commands will make lists ..." So they will make the lists with the number of days and the bonuses for each member individually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand that. Can you tell me, though, who the command is. Would you be part of the PJP command who would make a list or is it at some higher level?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done in the detachments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you're interested in learning about my unit, I can tell you about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I am interested in that, but I'm also interested in trying to finish in the next 15 minutes or so, so let me go on to something else. Thank you. Exhibit D61, this was a document that made reference to, I think, the foreign experts who were going to try to participate in an exhumation at Gornje Obrinje. You remember that one?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember this case, if I may call it that, not the details but there is mention of Mr. Kari Korklo a forensic expert from Finland; but I couldn't give you any more details. I remember that because I was involved in providing escort to them and making sure that everything goes as planned and I think that I've already explained to you how it actually unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. In connection with Gornje Obrinje, were you aware that in late September 1998, around the 26th of September, that MUP forces were crushing and destroying the KLA in that area, and they were supported by the VJ, and that three policemen had been killed by the KLA close to Gornje Obrinje on that date? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember the activity itself, but I do remember that there were some anti-terrorist tasks in that area, the narrower area and the more general area. Probably what you're saying is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did you -- do you recall that there was a lot of public outcry in the international community and that later on there was a Human Rights Watch report written about Gornje Obrinje with allegations that Serb forces had killed at least 21 members of a particular family of Kosovo Albanian civilians, including women and children ? Do you remember hearing about that back then?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think so from the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You probably were aware of that, but you may not have been aware of a VJ report from General Pavkovic suggesting that the Pristina Corps security department had information that unidentified members of MUP units had executed civilians taken into custody during that operation in the Gornje Obrinje area. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of the details that you've just put to me. Before and after the war, I did not go to that area. I think it territorially belongs to the municipality of Glogovac, but you can't go there through the municipality of Glogovac, you have to go through Srbica if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. You were asked about whether the police administration of the MUP in the PJP department there was a section for the preparation of defence plans, page 36, line 6, today you said: "A. I believe so." Were you aware of Instructions for the Defence of Inhabited or Populated Areas that had been issued by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija in July of 1998? Did you ever see or hear of those?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will be quick. The first part was put to the witness correctly, that pertains to the defence plans in the police administration, and now the question pertains to completely different kind of defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you need me to repeat the question? Did you ever see or hear of a document called: Instructions for the Defence of Populated or Inhabited Areas, issued by the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija in July 1998?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You were asked a question about volunteers earlier today. You said there were never -- well, as far as MUP was concerned you said: " ... we did not receive any volunteers." Would you allow for the possibility that there may have been volunteers taken into the MUP that you didn't hear about?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that answering the questions today I said that when I meant the MUP I meant the secretariat where I worked, not the entire ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that clarification.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we look quickly at Exhibit P688. And I think we need to go to page 7 in the English and page 6 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic asked you about this earlier today where Colonel Petric was talking about the situation in Pristina. I don't know if that's on your B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Is that it now?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Maybe Mr. Djurdjic can help me find that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's the wrong minutes because Colonel Filic was there. Please tell me what you have in mind, and I'll immediately tell you. Was it the 22nd of July?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I had Exhibit 688 --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that -- what is the date, Mr. Hannis, if you can tell me then I'll be able to assist you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, the English is the correct one, the bottom of page 7 on the English in this document K053-4159.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 688.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can you help us with where in that document in the B/C/S is that speech by Colonel Petric followed immediately by Captain Pesic?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have it now in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Captain Pesic is reporting about: "We formed 243 reserve police stations ..." And then it talks about the number of weapons that have been issued between the VJ to some 34 almost 35.000 people and some that have been issued by the MUP. At the end he says: "When all of this is finished, about 60.000 persons will have been issued weapons." Those were Serbs who had been issued weapons, weren't they, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Blagoje Pesic, he informed or briefed those present. I assume that the weapons were issued mostly to Serbs, but I am absolutely sure that there were cases when it was issued also to Albanians, Roma, and other people living there in the villages and towns where the weapons were distributed, but I'm sure that in the latter case those were sporadic cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. At page 59 today Mr. Djurdjic asked you a series of questions about whether you had issued any orders or were aware of any orders or knew about Kosovo Albanian civilians being killed or forced to leave Pristina or turn over their personal documents, and you answered no you didn't know anything about any of that. Can you tell us where were you physically located between the 24th of March and the 15th of June, 1999? What percentage of your time was out in the field versus when you were in Pristina, like we know you were when you attended meetings? Do you have any idea how much time was in Pristina and how much time was out in the field somewhere else approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that I will be able to tell you that with any certainty. I spent very little time in Pristina. I tried to explain what my duties were at the time, that I would spend more time out in the field, so I couldn't really give you a percentage. I would be wrong in doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. It sounds like you were out in the field more than half the time; would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes. Probably even more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And at page 61, line 4, today you gave an answer about the presence of Kosovo Albanian civilians during anti-terrorist actions. You said you couldn't answer with a hundred per cent certainty; but in all the anti-terrorist actions that you took part in, there were no civilians in the inhabited area where the fighting was going on. The population had been evacuated you assume by the KLA. Did you never surprise the KLA when you attacked these villages and towns where they were? How did they manage always to have the civilians out of the way before you attacked them?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first I have to say that we did not attack towns and villages. When somebody mounts a defence, the defence is not mounted in the village itself. You set it up on dominant heights. Now, if you ask me how that is possible, I assume that before a task was launched or after a task was executed, that the population would be evacuated or would seek shelter. But I don't think that there were any secrets about our activities. So I think that was behind it more than anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: During the time-period March 24th through mid-June/early June when the war ended, while you were out in the field did you not see large numbers of Kosovo Albanian civilians on the roads leading out of Kosovo towards Macedonia and Albania?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that I saw any large columns because for the most part I was in the woods not near the roads. But had I known that this was going on, or rather, if you ask me if I knew that this was going on, yes, I did know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. How did you know about it?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, simply, it was not a secret.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. The last thing I want to ask you, first thing today you were asked about your knowledge of General Djordjevic's presence in Kosovo in 1999. And if I understood your answer right, you mentioned seeing General Djordjevic at a meeting on the 17th of February and then the only other time you saw him was in June, right around the time the Kumanovo Agreement was signed. Is that your testimony now? Am I stating it correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But in your witness statement that you made in -- five years ago, in 2004, on the 6th and 7th of May, paragraph 26 you said: "Generals Vlastimir Djordjevic and Obrad Stevanovic did visit Kosovo in 1999 on a regular basis." That sounds like more than two times. Why have you changed your answer from what you said in May 2004?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not change my answer. The question was when I saw General Obrad Stevanovic and General Vlastimir Djordjevic and at the beginning of my evidence here I said that I could see them because it was my position at the time, what it was, and I could see them either at meetings or in the field. The fact is that on the basis of what we have seen over the past few days, General Obrad Stevanovic's presence there was much greater. And this is why I said that they were there more often because they attended all the meetings, and in the previous case that was not the case. So that was just a clarification of my previous evidence. I still have the same opinion and there was only one question then on that topic and I more or less gave you the answer that you've just quoted to me without going into any details who, how, when.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Was your memory for events in 1999 better five years ago than it is today, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: ZARKO BRAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there is a possibility when it comes to some minor details or incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll be pleased to know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Brakovic, that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would thank you for your attendance once again in The Hague and the assistance you've been able to give us, and you may now, of course, return to your normal activities. The court officer will assist you when we rise. We now adjourn for the day to resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much and all the best.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 12th day of May, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.
